Alex: quick heads-up — i'm sketching a change to the model intake surface. we need to nail down what 'dependency surface' means between the ML onboarding/benching team and runtime. want quick sync on contract shape. :wave:
Jamie: +1. are you talking about artifacts (onnx/quant binaries) vs runtime hints (seqlen, kv-behavior)?
Alex: exactly. current problem: teams produce binaries with implicit runtime expectations (kv layout, aten ops, fused kernels) and runtime ends up guessing. leads to subtle perf regressions on dedicated pools.
Marta: can you give an example? i missed the last incident.
Alex: last week model X passed smoke but failed perf targets under 8k token regen because worker selected a fallback kernel that didn't support our fused attention pattern. bench had short sequences; runtime saw long tails in prod.
Samir: ugh. so bench sampling didn't mirror prod seqlen distribution. that's on us.
Lia: this is why we wanted an explicit "execution_hints" field in the manifest. small JSON with: {"expected_max_seq": 8192, "kv_layout": "kv-v2", "prefer_fused": true, "ops_blacklist": []}. runtime can use that to pick kernels and quantization profile fallback.
Jamie: love the idea. two clarifying q's: 1) do we enforce hints as mandatory (block) or advisory? 2) who owns correctness if hints disagree with detected characteristics at runtime?
Marta: for (1) my vote is staged enforcement: advisory during early onboarding (smoke + mini-bench), mandatory for "dedicated" promotion. blocks for hosted until we have auto-detect.
Samir: staged enforcement sounds practical. add a checksum field for the binary + stable-abi tag so runtime can refuse unknown ABI variants in strict mode.
Alex: proposal: manifest schema v1 with fields: artifact_checksum, abi_tag, execution_hints, golden_inputs (list of sample prompts), perf_targets {p50_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec} and a signed provenance blob. runtime uses policy: if jurisdiction == strict or customer_tier == enterprise => treat mismatches as failure; else log + fallback.
Lia: we should also standardize a mini-bench harness contract: sample size, seed list, and target host config (like a CPU/GPU flavor). mini-bench should run in CI and upload a compact perf summary to the registry.
Jamie: how expensive is mini-bench? teams will fight cost.
Marta: keep mini-bench cheap: 10 warmup runs + 50 measured samples across seeded prompts at two seqlen points (short/long). only measure p50/p95 and peak mem. full bench remains nightly on benches.
Samir: also add a KV smoke: run a short multi-turn that exercises cache population + retrieval latency. that caught the fused attention problem earlier.
Alex: decision A: add execution_hints and artifact_checksum in manifest v1. enforcement: advisory for hosted normal, strict for dedicated/private by default. Decision B: define mini-bench contract (cheap, deterministic seeds) as part of onboarding checklist.
Jamie: can we automate bolt-on checks in the ingestion pipeline? e.g., if manifest says prefer_fused=true but runtime reports fused not available -> fail build or tag?
Lia: ingestion pipeline can run a capability probe against target runtime image and annotate the model registry with "capabilities_ok": true/false. if false, mark as "needs_runtime-adaptation" and kick to bench-team.
Marta: action items: 1) Alex to draft manifest schema PR and example. 2) Samir to add mini-bench harness spec and seed list. 3) Lia to prototype capability probe and registry flag.
Alex: assigned. i'll post the PR by EOD. any objections?
Jamie: no objections. one ask: add migration path for existing models — do not break older artifacts.
Alex: will include migration section: runtime will map missing fields to safe defaults and emit prominent warnings until models are re-ingested.
BuildBot: automated check: attached CI job 'ingest-smoke' passed for current branch (job 98431). :white_check_mark:
Samir: tiny nit — include a field "bench_suite_version" in manifest to tie mini-bench results to the schema.
Lia: yep, good call. also include provenance signer (git sha / builder image).
Marta: thanks all. i think this reduces ambiguity a lot. can folks ack when they see Alex's PR?
Jamie: ack, i'll review. :eyes:
Samir: ack
Lia: ack
Alex: thanks — will follow up in the PR with examples and a minimal reference loader snippet:
Alex: ```python
# pseudo loader
def load_manifest(path):
    m = json.load(open(path))
    verify_checksum(m['artifact_checksum'])
    if m['execution_hints'].get('prefer_fused') and not runtime.capability('fused_attention'):
        runtime.annotate('capability_mismatch', True)
    return m
```
Alex: closing thread after PR posted, will re-open if we need infra changes. :v:
